Getting started with VIGAT

Source: vignettes/VIGAT.Rmd
VIGAT.Rmd

Overview

Gene activity scores for single-cell ATAC-seq are usually computed by counting fragments over a fixed region for every gene, such as the gene body plus 2 kb upstream. A fixed rule can miss where the informative accessibility actually is: the cell-type-specific signal may sit in a short promoter peak, be offset from the annotated TSS, or be mixed with signal from a neighbouring gene.

VIGAT (VLM-guided gene activity quantification) chooses the region gene by gene, the way an analyst would by eye. For each marker gene it

  1. draws a coverage plot of the ±5 kb around the TSS, with one track per ATAC cluster, the gene model and the called peaks;
  2. sends the plots to a vision-language model (VLM) with instructions to pick one compact window that captures the clearest cluster-specific promoter signal;
  3. uses the selected windows to quantify ATAC fragments and construct a gene-by-cell activity matrix, without requiring explicit cell type annotations.

All of this happens in a single call to VIGAT().

This vignette runs VIGAT on a human pancreatic islet sample with 15 marker genes for 7 cell types.

Installation 

install.packages(c("Seurat", "Signac", "remotes"))
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("GenomicRanges", "GenomeInfoDb", "IRanges",
                       "S4Vectors", "BiocGenerics"))
remotes::install_github("beijie02/VIGAT")

Set up your OpenAI API key

VIGAT sends the coverage plots to the OpenAI API, so you need your own OpenAI API key.

  1. Sign in at https://platform.openai.com, open the API keys page and create a new secret key. API usage is billed to your OpenAI account, so add a payment method or credits under Billing before running VIGAT.
  2. Assign the key in R before calling VIGAT():
# IMPORTANT! Assign your OpenAI API key
Sys.setenv(OPENAI_API_KEY = "your_openai_API_key")

This sets the key for the current R session only. To set it permanently, add the following line to the file ~/.Renviron (create the file if it does not exist; usethis::edit_r_environ() opens it for you) and restart R:

OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_API_key

You can check that R sees the key with nchar(Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")) > 0. If the key is missing, VIGAT() stops with an error explaining how to set it.

⚠️ Warning: avoid sharing your API key with others or uploading it to public spaces. Do not write the key into scripts you share, and do not commit .Renviron to GitHub.

Load packages 

library(VIGAT)
library(Seurat)
library(Signac)

Example data

The example is the human islet sample GSM7618328_GSM7618327 from CompassDB. The object has been quality-controlled and clustered on the ATAC data, and the cluster labels are stored in the metadata column ATAC_cluster.

Three files are needed: the object islet_example_atac.rds (about 3.9 GB), the fragment file islet_fragments.tsv.gz (about 3.1 GB) and its index islet_fragments.tsv.gz.tbi. They are deposited on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23347228). Download them into the same folder:

options(timeout = 3600)   # large files: allow up to an hour per download
base  <- "https://zenodo.org/records/23347228/files"
files <- c("islet_example_atac.rds",
           "islet_fragments.tsv.gz",
           "islet_fragments.tsv.gz.tbi")

for (f in files) {
  download.file(paste0(base, "/", f, "?download=1"), f, mode = "wb")
}

A Signac object stores the location of its fragment file, so point the object to the downloaded file:

obj <- readRDS("islet_example_atac.rds")

frags <- Fragments(obj)
frags[[1]] <- UpdatePath(frags[[1]], new.path = "islet_fragments.tsv.gz")
Fragments(obj) <- NULL
Fragments(obj) <- frags

table(obj$ATAC_cluster)

The object has 10,093 cells in 8 ATAC clusters. To make the results easier to read, the table below labels each cluster with the RNA cell type that most of its cells belong to. VIGAT does not use these labels; the model only sees the cluster numbers.

ATAC cluster Cells Majority RNA cell type
0 5,796 Beta cell
1 2,485 Alpha cell
2 707 Delta cell
3 276 TUBA1A ductal cell
4 272 Fibroblast
5 262 Endothelial cell
6 221 Alpha cell
7 74 Acinar cell

Marker genes

For each cell type present in the sample we use two or three marker genes, taken from the cell type markers in DISCO.

Cell type Marker genes
Acinar cell CPA1, CTRB1, PRSS1
Alpha cell GCG, TTR
Beta cell IAPP, INS
Delta cell RBP4, SST
Endothelial cell PECAM1, RAMP2
Fibroblast DCN, LUM
TUBA1A ductal cell SERPINA1, SPP1 
marker_genes <- c("CPA1", "CTRB1", "PRSS1",      # acinar
                  "GCG", "TTR",                 # alpha
                  "IAPP", "INS",                # beta
                  "RBP4", "SST",                # delta
                  "PECAM1", "RAMP2",            # endothelial
                  "DCN", "LUM",                 # fibroblast
                  "SERPINA1", "SPP1")           # ductal

Run VIGAT

One call does the whole analysis:

res <- VIGAT(
  obj         = obj,
  genes       = marker_genes,
  tissue      = "Islet",
  species     = "human",
  cluster_col = "ATAC_cluster",
  return_highlighted_plots = TRUE
)

Inside VIGAT():

  • Cells with no cluster label are removed, and so are clusters with fewer than min_atac_cluster_cells cells (50 by default). Here every cluster has at least 50 cells, so all 10,093 cells are kept.
  • For each gene, the TSS and strand are taken from the gene annotation of the ATAC assay, and the called peaks within ±5 kb are collected.
  • The coverage plots are laid out four genes per page and uploaded to the model as PDFs, together with a prompt that lists each gene, its strand and the overlapping peaks. The PDFs are written to a temporary folder and deleted when VIGAT() returns.
  • The model returns one window per gene. The selected regions are then used to quantify ATAC fragments and construct a gene-by-cell activity matrix, without requiring explicit cell type annotations. The counting uses Signac::FeatureMatrix() (see Gene activity matrix below).

VIGAT() writes nothing to disk; everything comes back in res. The main outputs are res$vigat_windows, the selected window for each gene, and res$count_matrix, the gene-by-cell activity matrix of fragment counts in those windows.

In this run the model (gpt-5.5) used 38,082 tokens and took about 2.1 minutes for 15 genes, sent as 4 PDF pages.

Selected windows

res$vigat_windows is a GRanges object with one window per gene, and res$vigat_window_df holds the same information as a data frame. The model also explains each choice; its reply is kept in res$diagnostics$raw_response. The table below combines the two.

Gene Strand Window Width (bp) Anchor evidence Strongest clusters Model rationale
CPA1 + chr7:130,379,450-130,381,100 1651 called Peak chr7:130379537-130381024 clusters 7, 1, 2, 3 Promoter-side/TSS-proximal peak for the + strand gene, with clear acinar-like cluster-specific accessibility, especially cluster 7.
CTRB1 + chr16:75,218,250-75,219,250 1001 called Peak chr16:75218572-75219094 clusters 7, 5, 4 Compact window around the promoter-overlapping called peak just upstream of the + strand TSS, avoiding more distal weak signal.
PRSS1 + chr7:142,748,850-142,749,850 1001 called Peak chr7:142749214-142749495 clusters 7, 3 Sharp promoter-side accessibility overlapping the called peak near the + strand TSS.
GCG − chr2:162,152,004-162,153,004 1001 called Peak overlapping the TSS (inside the window) clusters 1, 6 TSS-overlapping window at the - strand GCG promoter that captures the alpha-like signal in clusters 1 and 6, avoiding the strong upstream peak shared by most clusters.
TTR + chr18:31,590,850-31,592,050 1201 called Peak chr18:31590941-31591981 clusters 1, 0, 2, 3 TSS-proximal/promoter peak with strong cluster-specific accessibility; avoids distal downstream/upstream peaks.
IAPP + chr12:21,353,250-21,354,350 1101 called Peak chr12:21353327-21354299 clusters 0, 6, 5, 2 Promoter-side peak immediately upstream of the + strand IAPP TSS; avoids the more distal left peak likely less specific to IAPP.
INS − chr11:2,160,750-2,161,750 1001 called Peak chr11:2160857-2161482 cluster 0 Promoter/TSS-proximal peak for the - strand INS locus, capturing the strongest useful promoter signal while avoiding distal TH-side peaks.
RBP4 − chr10:93,599,850-93,601,750 1901 called Peak chr10:93599896-93601663 clusters 0, 2, 3, 5, 6 Broad but compact TSS-proximal/promoter-overlapping signal at the RBP4 end of the locus; avoids the more distal upstream peak.
SST − chr3:187,669,650-187,670,850 1201 called Peak chr3:187669747-187670768 clusters 2, 3, 4, 7 Promoter-side peak overlapping the - strand SST TSS region, with strong cluster-specific signal.
PECAM1 − chr17:64,411,750-64,412,750 1001 called Peak chr17:64411826-64412481 cluster 5 The canonical upstream/right-side peak is weak in the marker-like cluster, so this compact TSS-adjacent/proximal intragenic peak was selected because it gives the clearest PECAM1-specific signal.
RAMP2 + chr17:42,760,450-42,761,950 1501 called Peak chr17:42760516-42761934 cluster 5 Selected the clearest proximal RAMP2-associated accessible region overlapping a called peak; the immediate upstream promoter-side signal is weak.
DCN − chr12:91,180,323-91,181,523 1201 coverage-only cluster 4 No called peak overlaps the informative signal; compact intragenic window over the fibroblast-like coverage in cluster 4, avoiding the distal left-side signal shared across clusters.
LUM − chr12:91,110,950-91,111,950 1001 called Peak chr12:91111385-91111750 clusters 4, 6, 7 Promoter/TSS-proximal peak for the - strand LUM gene, capturing the clearest local accessibility.
SERPINA1 − chr14:94,390,200-94,391,200 1001 called Peak chr14:94390440-94391068 clusters 3, 7, 2 Promoter-side peak overlapping the - strand SERPINA1 TSS region; avoids the more downstream/internal peak.
SPP1 + chr4:87,974,650-87,975,850 1201 called Peak chr4:87974783-87975774 clusters 3, 7, 0, 2, 4 TSS-proximal promoter-side peak for the + strand gene with strong, compact accessibility; avoids the more distal downstream gene-body peak.

All 15 genes received a window between 1.0 and 1.9 kb. Fourteen are anchored on a called peak; for DCN no peak overlaps the informative signal, so the window follows the coverage alone.

The strongest clusters named by the model agree with the cell-type labels above without the model having seen them: acinar genes (CPA1, CTRB1, PRSS1) point to cluster 7, INS to cluster 0 (beta), PECAM1 and RAMP2 to cluster 5 (endothelial), and DCN to cluster 4 (fibroblast).

Save the results

Because VIGAT() does not write files, save what you need yourself:

saveRDS(res, "vigat_islet_result.rds")
write.csv(res$vigat_window_df, "vigat_windows.csv", row.names = FALSE)

for (g in names(res$highlighted_plots)) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(g, "_vigat.png"), res$highlighted_plots[[g]],
                  width = 11, height = 11, dpi = 150)
}

Model replies can differ slightly between runs, so keep the saved result (including res$vigat_windows) for the analysis you report.

Inspect intermediate results

Set return_intermediates = TRUE to also get the inputs VIGAT built for the model:

res <- VIGAT(obj, genes = marker_genes, tissue = "Islet",
             cluster_col = "ATAC_cluster", return_intermediates = TRUE)

res$intermediates$tss_info           # TSS, strand and plotted region per gene
res$intermediates$overlapping_peaks  # called peaks inside each region
res$intermediates$coverage_plots     # the plots sent to the model
cat(res$intermediates$prompt)        # the full prompt
res$intermediates$api_run_info       # model, tokens, time

Options

Argument Default Description
obj (required) Signac Seurat object with an ATAC assay, gene annotation and fragment files
genes (required) Marker genes to score
tissue (required) Tissue name given to the model as context, e.g. "Islet"
species "human" Species given to the model; NULL omits it
cluster_col NULL Metadata column with ATAC clusters; NULL uses Idents(obj)
min_atac_cluster_cells 50 Clusters with fewer cells are removed before plotting
openai_model "gpt-5.5" OpenAI model that reads the plots
return_intermediates FALSE Also return TSS info, peaks, input coverage plots, prompt and API logs
return_highlighted_plots FALSE Also return one coverage plot per gene with the selected window highlighted
